$schema_note: Maps every byte offset (0-63) of each report shape to a named field. Checked by bin/ci against fixtures/*.json for full coverage. Reassembly across multiple physical reports is NOT modeled here because discovery found there isn't any: opcodes 0x40/0x41/0x42 are independently complete report types, not fragments of one larger logical message (see PROTOCOL.md).

fields.name: length
fields.meaning: length of the info-package array that follows (magic+cmd+subfields+inner-crc)

fields.name: checksum16le
fields.formula: sum = (opcode + byte1 + byte2 + length + 0 + 0 + 0 + sum(payload_bytes)) & 0xFFFF, stored as [sum&0xFF, (sum>>8)&0xFF]. Bytes 1-2 are part of the sum: they are zero for every command except picture-upload bulk packets, where they carry the data offset. Bytes 4-6 count as zero while summing (the vendor builds the array with 0x00 placeholders there, computes the sum, then writes the two checksum bytes back into 4 and 5).

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: 0x00 on outbound request, 0x55 on device ACK (getDongleAndKeyboardStatus opcode reused as an ack marker)

fields.name: payload_then_padding
fields.meaning: the info-package array (length bytes, command-specific, see commands below), then 0x00 padding to offset 63

fields.name: dataOffsetLE16
fields.meaning: Byte offset of this packet's payload within the whole data stream being uploaded, little-endian. Zero for every short command (set-time's data packets, picture-upload's declare-size), which is why Phase 0 recorded these two bytes as 'reserved'. Milestone 3's bulk pixel packets walk it 0, 56, 112, ... 30688.

fields.name: length
fields.meaning: length of the data payload that follows

fields.name: checksum16le
fields.formula: sum = (opcode + byte1 + byte2 + length + 0 + 0 + 0 + sum(payload_bytes)) & 0xFFFF, stored as [sum&0xFF, (sum>>8)&0xFF]. Bytes 1-2 are part of the sum: they are zero for every command except picture-upload bulk packets, where they carry the data offset. Bytes 4-6 count as zero while summing (the vendor builds the array with 0x00 placeholders there, computes the sum, then writes the two checksum bytes back into 4 and 5).
fields.correction: Milestone 3: this was previously documented as an 8-bit checksum at byte 4 with a reserved zero at byte 5. Byte 4 was always right -- it is the low byte either way -- but byte 5 is the HIGH byte, not a reserved zero. Every command decoded before Milestone 3 had a total sum below 256, so the old model produced identical bytes and looked correct. In fixtures/picture-upload.json, byte 5 is non-zero in 551 of 552 reports.

fields.name: payload_then_padding
fields.meaning: the data payload (length bytes, command-specific, see commands below), then 0x00 padding

fields.name: length
fields.note: always 56 for this opcode in every capture; the site calls it with no explicit payload -- 56 is a baked-in constant, not derived from an actual 56-byte payload. Numeric meaning of 56 itself is unresolved (see unresolved[]).

fields.name: checksum16le
fields.formula: sum = (opcode + byte1 + byte2 + length + 0 + 0 + 0 + sum(payload_bytes)) & 0xFFFF, stored as [sum&0xFF, (sum>>8)&0xFF]. Bytes 1-2 are part of the sum: they are zero for every command except picture-upload bulk packets, where they carry the data offset. Bytes 4-6 count as zero while summing (the vendor builds the array with 0x00 placeholders there, computes the sum, then writes the two checksum bytes back into 4 and 5).
fields.note: Always [0x7a, 0x00] for this constant report -- its sum (0x42 + 0x38 = 0x7a) is below 256, so the high byte is zero. See the 0x41 correction note.

fields.name: padding
fields.meaning: always all-zero in every observed capture

infoPackagePayload.note: [magic 0xA5 0x5A, cmd=9, 0x00, len=3, innerCrc16(0x09,0x00,0x03)] -- innerCrc16 uses a SEPARATE CRC-16/ARC function (poly 0xA001 reflected, init 0xFFFF), precomputed by the vendor's bundler since inputs never change. Do not confuse with the outer report checksum above.

[magic, cmd=11, 0x00, len=0, innerCrc16(0x0B,0x00,0x00)] -- no data-packet follows (unlike cmd9/cmd10, N=0). Resolved Milestone 2 (2026-08-11) via live HID capture; see fixtures/page-switch.json and fixtures/raw/cap-page-switch-hidlog.json.

cmd11_switchToHomepage.note: "Switch to the homepage" button. Sequence: infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42), no data-packet, no repeat loop.

cmd13_switchToPicturePage.note: "Switch to the picture page" button. Same 2-report shape as cmd11.

cmd15_switchToGifPage.note: "Switch to the GIF page" button. Same info+finish shape as cmd11/cmd13. The bytes are correct and were always correct. Milestone 2 recorded that this command did not visibly switch the panel and filed it as unresolved; Milestone 3 found the real cause, and it was not this command -- the GIF under test had only ever been saved in the vendor's mode 0 ("set as boot animation"), which stores frames somewhere with no known way to make them play (the known activation steps -- the GIF page, power-up/replug -- don't show it; the search hasn't been exhaustive). Saved in mode 1 ("save to the device"), the GIF displays and cmd15 switches to it. Milestone 4 ships it as `switch-page gif`, together with `set-gif`. (The old "see unresolved[0]" pointer is gone: that entry was resolved and removed, and index 0 now holds an unrelated item. Never cite an unresolved entry by index -- the list is reordered whenever something is resolved.)

cmd14_clearPicture.note: "Clear the picture" button. Same info+finish shape as cmd11/13/15, but sent 16x in a row (32 reports total) -- matches the vendor source's literal for(a=0;a<16;a++) loop, and independently confirmed by counting the full raw HID log (not just trusting the source). Structurally UNRELATED to "Clear GIF" despite the vendor's internal function name for this loop implying otherwise -- see cmd18_clearGif/cmd19_clearGif (resolved Milestone 7) and scripts/vendor-source-excerpt.js's corrective note.

infoPackagePayload.note: EIGHT bytes, not the seven every command decoded before it: [magic, cmd=16, 0x00, len=1, innerCrc16(0x10,0x00,0x01), 0x01]. The trailing 0x01 is the one-byte body the len=1 field describes. Resolved Milestone 3 (2026-08-11). Constant across every picture upload captured, because the panel size is fixed.

cmd16_pictureUploadStart.note: Opens a picture upload. In the vendor's GIF path the equivalent per-frame command carries a mode byte and a frame index in place of that trailing 0x01, which is why this payload is documented as a picture-upload constant rather than as the general shape of cmd16.

dataPacketPayload.note: [magic, cmd=12, 0x78, 0x00, innerCrc16(0x0C,0x78,0x00)]. `120,0` is 30720 -- the total pixel-stream length -- encoded [hi,lo], the opposite order from the LE offset in bytes 1-2 of the same report. Constant only because the panel is a fixed 160x96; a device with a different panel would send a different value here.

cmd12_pictureDeclareSize.note: Declares how many bytes of pixel data will follow. Sent as a data packet (0x41), not an info package (0x40) -- the only command so far whose leading report is a 0x41.

dataPacketPayload.note: GIF session OPEN and CLOSE -- NOT a "clear GIF" command, which is how Milestone 2 filed it. Nine bytes: the fixed prefix [magic, cmd=18, 0x00, len=2, innerCrc16(0x12,0x00,0x02)] followed by two parameters. Byte 7 is the save MODE; byte 8 is 0 on open and the FRAME COUNT on close. The inner CRC covers only [18,0,2] -- the two trailing bytes sit after it and are NOT inputs to it, they are covered by the outer checksum like any other payload byte. OPCODE QUIRK: the opening cmd18 is sent as an info package (0x40) while the closing one is a data packet (0x41); Milestone 2's "Clear GIF" capture sent both as 0x40, so those samples are a different sequence and not a cross-check for these.

cmd18_gifSession.note: Resolved Milestone 4 (2026-08-11) from a real mode-1 save of a 2-frame GIF.

dataPacketPayload.note: The second half of the GIF session pair. Same shape as cmd18; byte 8 is 0 on open and the FRAME RATE on close (the vendor's slider is 1-60, default 30, so a 30 fps save closes with 0x1e). Sent as a data packet (0x41) both times.

infoPackagePayload.note: "Clear GIF" button, Equipment setup tab. Shares a cmd number AND opcode (0x40, info-package) with cmd18_gifSession's OPEN form -- disambiguated by the payload length-nibble byte (1 here, no variable trailer; 2 there, prefix + 2-byte trailer). Does NOT match cmd18_gifSession's shape at all beyond the shared cmd number: different length nibble, different trailer bytes ([5,16,1,0] here vs the [4,80] open/close constant there). Resolved Milestone 7 (2026-08-12), live capture, 3 independent captures confirmed deterministic (2 out-only, 1 full duplex with real device ACKs).

The second half of "Clear GIF". Byte-identical to cmd19_gifSessionRate's dataPacketPayload prefix + a [mode=1, last=0] trailer -- almost certainly coincidental vendor reuse, not a documented relationship. Sent as an info-package (0x40), unlike cmd19_gifSessionRate which is always a data-packet (0x41) in both its open and close forms -- this is the one detail that actually disambiguates it, since the byte content alone is identical to a normal session-open's cmd19 half.

dataPacketPayload.note: Same inner command number as picture upload's start (cmd 16) but a different command: len=3 with a three-byte trailer, sent as a data packet (0x41) rather than an info package (0x40), and repeated once per frame with a 0-based frame index in the last byte.
Declares one FRAME's byte count, sent once per frame straight after cmd16. `120,0` is 30720 as [hi,lo], the same encoding cmd12 uses for the whole picture.

transactionStructure.note: One 'Update device time' click = a for-loop of 3 iterations (confirmed in vendor source), each iteration sending: cmd9 infoPackage(0x40) -> cmd9 dataPacket(0x41) -> finish(0x42) -> cmd10 infoPackage(0x40) -> cmd10 dataPacket(0x41) -> finish(0x42). Every outbound report receives exactly 2 identical inputreport ACKs from the device (byte offset 6 flipped 0x00->0x55, otherwise byte-identical to the request) AS OBSERVED VIA WEBHID -- see rawEventCounts below for the counted evidence behind that. IMPORTANT: this is the WebHID-transport count; see linuxHidrawTransport below -- at the native hidraw layer only 1 real ACK arrives per write, not 2.

pageSwitch.shape: infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42) -- 2 reports total, no data-packet, no repeat loop.

clearPicture.shape: The 2-report infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42) pair, repeated 16 times (32 reports total) -- matches the vendor source's literal for(a=0;a<16;a++) loop. All 16 repeats are byte-identical (the command carries no per-iteration state), the same way set-time's 3 repeats are.
clearPicture.resolvedBy: Milestone 2, live HID capture + full raw-log event count, 2026-08-11.

clearGif.shape: 4 reports: cmd18's infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42), then cmd19's infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42) -- two DIFFERENT payloads, no repeat loop (unlike clear-picture's 16x). No deliberate delay between any of the 4 reports (0-7ms gaps observed, ordinary HID round-trip time) -- unlike picture-upload's 300ms pause or GIF-upload's host sleeps.
clearGif.resolvedBy: Milestone 7, live HID capture (real device ACKs, not flip-derived), 3 independent captures confirmed deterministic, 2026-08-12.

pictureUpload.shape: 552 reports: infoPackage(0x40 cmd16) -> [host sleeps 300 ms] -> dataPacket(0x41 cmd12, declare size) -> 549x dataPacket(0x41) carrying the pixel stream -> finish(0x42). The bulk packets carry 56 bytes each EXCEPT the last, which carries 32 and declares 32 -- see bulkPackets below; do not restate this as "56 bytes each", which is the mistake an earlier draft made. The 300 ms pause sits between the start report and declare-size, NOT before the bulk data: that is the order in the vendor's own source (`await r(re); await sleep(300); await o(Ue); ...`) and it is where the gap appears in the captured timestamps.

bulkPackets.note: 56 = the vendor's `reqLen - 7`, i.e. the report size minus the 7-byte header. Bytes 1-2 carry the little-endian offset (0, 56, ... 30688). The length byte is the REAL remaining byte count, so the last packet declares 0x20 (32), not a zero-padded 0x38: 548*56 + 32 = 30720 exactly. Getting that wrong also corrupts that packet's checksum, since the length byte is summed.

pixelFormat.encoding: RGB565, big-endian per pixel: v = (R>>3)<<11 | (G>>2)<<5 | (B>>3), emitted as [v>>8, v&0xFF]. Row-major, top row first, left to right. Fully transparent pixels are flattened to black before encoding. Total 30720 bytes, always.
pixelFormat.resize: The vendor draws the source through a canvas with imageSmoothingEnabled = false, i.e. nearest-neighbour. An interpolating resize produces different bytes for the same input.
pixelFormat.verifiedBy: fixtures/picture-upload.json is regenerated from fixtures/test-quadrants.png through these rules and compared against the real capture in fixtures/raw/cap-picture-upload-hidlog.json by scripts/check-raw-consistency.js: 0 mismatches across all 552 reports / 30720 pixel bytes. A four-quadrant + gradient image was used precisely because solid colours cannot distinguish row order, channel order, or per-pixel byte order.
pixelFormat.alpha: The vendor's PICTURE encoder reads only bytes 0-2 of each RGBA quad and never looks at alpha: `function te(J){const ae=J.data; ... const xe=ae[he],ve=ae[he+1],re=ae[he+2]; ...}`. Its source is a getImageData() off a FRESH canvas -- no black fill -- and drawing source-over onto a transparent backdrop preserves the un-premultiplied colour. So a semi-transparent pixel contributes its FULL RGB, and only a fully transparent pixel comes back as (0,0,0,0), i.e. black. This is NOT premultiplication (`out = src*a`), which a cross-review reading of the plan's prose suggested; the `if (data[i+3] === 0)` black pre-pass that does exist belongs to the vendor's GIF path, not this one.

pictureUpload.resolvedBy: Milestone 3, live HID capture of the vendor tool + source read, 2026-08-11.

gifUpload.shape: 1149 reports for a 2-frame GIF: infoPackage(0x40 cmd18) + dataPacket(0x41 cmd19) to open the session, then per frame [dataPacket(0x41 cmd16 frame header) -> dataPacket(0x41 cmd17 declare 30720) -> 30 blocks x 19 bulk packets], then dataPacket(0x41 cmd18 frame count) + dataPacket(0x41 cmd19 fps) to close, then finish(0x42). Count = 2 + frames*(2 + 30*19) + 2 + 1.

blockChunking.note: THE KEY DIFFERENCE FROM PICTURE UPLOAD. A frame's 30720 bytes are pushed one 1024-byte block at a time, and each block is chunked independently, so the offset in bytes 1-2 RESTARTS AT 0 for every block and never reaches 1024. 1024 = 18*56 + 16, so a block is 19 packets whose last declares 16 bytes. Picture upload instead runs a single continuous offset 0..30688 across the whole frame. Milestone 3's prose said GIF 'reuses the same 56-byte bulk packets', which is true of the packet FORMAT and misleading about the chunker -- do not unify them.

modes.0: Set it as the startup animation. Max 64 frames, 160x96. Stores frames somewhere with no known way to make them play -- not on the GIF page, and not at power-up (tested by replugging), though the search hasn't been exhaustive. This is what misled Milestone 2 into believing cmd15 was broken. NOT implemented.
modes.1: Save to the device. Max 160 frames, 160x96. The mode that actually displays. THIS IS WHAT WE SHIP.
modes.2: Save GIF to the device home page. Max 42 frames, 96x64 (12288 bytes). The vendor renders this button only for productId 12463; this keyboard is 12744. Nothing on the wire enforces that, but it is a different frame size for a device we do not have. NOT implemented, NOT tested.

gifUpload.frameRate: One rate for the whole animation, sent once as the last byte of the closing cmd19. The vendor's slider is 1-60, default 30. A GIF with variable per-frame delays therefore cannot be reproduced exactly.
gifUpload.hostSleeps: 30 ms after the two open reports; 3000 ms after each frame's cmd16 when frameIndex % 16 == 0 (0-based, so frame 0 too) else 30 ms; nothing between cmd17 and the first block; 30 ms after EVERY 1024-byte block including the last; nothing between frames; 30 ms after each close report; and 500 ms before finish. The 3000 ms is almost certainly a flash-write pause.
gifUpload.pixelFormat: Identical to picture upload: 160x96 RGB565, big-endian per pixel, 30720 bytes per frame.
gifUpload.honestLimit: Unlike picture upload, this repo does NOT reproduce the vendor's pixel bytes. The vendor runs each GIF frame through a three-stage browser-canvas downscale with smoothing plus an edge filter, onto a black-filled canvas; browser resampling is implementation-defined and not reproducible outside a browser. This repo uses the same nearest-neighbour path as set-picture, so set-gif and set-picture agree with each other. What IS verified byte-for-byte against the capture: framing, ordering, block boundaries, per-block offsets, length bytes and every checksum -- see fixtures/gif-upload.json, which is a labelled hybrid.
gifUpload.resolvedBy: Milestone 4, live capture of a mode-1 save + vendor source read, 2026-08-11.

rawEventCounts.source: cap3 session, full window.__hidLog for one click (54 raw HID events), counted directly (not sampled) before deduplication into fixtures/cap3.json's representative-per-type entries
rawEventCounts.arithmeticCheck: sum(outCounts) = 3+3+6+3+3 = 18; sum(inCounts) = 6+6+12+6+6 = 36; 18+36 = 54, matching the raw log's total event count exactly -- every out report received exactly 2 in ACKs (inCount = 2 * outCount for every report type).

linuxInterfaceIdentity.note: Obtained directly via Linux shell access on the capture machine (not from browser JS -- the earlier draft of this phase incorrectly deferred this as unreachable; it only required a local shell, which was available all along).

configChannel.hidrawNode: /dev/hidraw5 (this machine, 2026-08-10 -- node numbers are not stable across reboots/replugs; re-identify by usage page/usage + descriptor hash, not by number)
configChannel.decodedDescriptor: Usage Page 0xFF60, Usage 0x61, Collection(Application): Usage 0x62 Input(count=64,size=8,data/var/abs), Usage 0x63 Output(count=64,size=8,data/var/abs). No Report ID item present -- confirms this is an unnumbered-report interface, consistent with WebHID's reportId:0.
configChannel.aclConfirmed: getfacl shows `user:ivan:rw-` on /dev/hidraw5, the config channel. IMPORTANT -- an earlier revision of this entry recorded 'confirmed for all 4 of the device's hidraw nodes, not just some' as a SUCCESS. That is backwards: interface 0 carries keystrokes, so user-readable access on all 4 nodes is a keylogger, not a healthy state. The repo's rule now matches interface 1 only, verified with `udevadm test` against all four interfaces (1 matches with GROUP plugdev and MODE 0660; 0, 2 and 3 do not). Note the ACLs observed on this machine come from systemd's own 73-seat-late.rules, not from this repo's rule, so seeing access on other interfaces here does not mean the rule is wrong -- check with `udevadm test`, never with getfacl alone.

allFourInterfaces.role: vendor config channel -- THIS is the one used for screen control
vendor-defined, input-only, 32-byte reports -- purpose not investigated, not used by screen control

linuxHidrawTransport.resolvedBy: Milestone 1 (native Rust set-time implementation), confirmed empirically against real hardware on 2026-08-10/11 -- see also the plan-review discussion where reviewers disagreed on the theoretical answer before this was tested.
linuxHidrawTransport.write: A native write() to /dev/hidraw5 requires a leading 0x00 'report number' byte prepended before the 64-byte report -- 65 bytes total on the wire. This is the documented Linux kernel hidraw behavior for unnumbered-report HID devices (the descriptor above has no Report ID item, yet the kernel still expects a synthetic ID byte on write). Writing exactly 64 bytes (no prefix) produces garbage responses from the device (observed: a status byte of 0x0f instead of the expected 0x00/0x55, on an otherwise-matching report) -- NOT silence, an actual malformed reply.
linuxHidrawTransport.read: read() returns exactly 64 bytes, WITHOUT the leading 0x00 -- asymmetric with write(). This matches the same documented kernel behavior (reads of unnumbered reports are not report-ID-prefixed).
linuxHidrawTransport.ackCount: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to Phase 0's WebHID-based finding: Phase 0's browser capture observed exactly 2 identical inputreport events per outbound report. At the native hidraw layer, only ONE real ACK arrives per write. The '2 ACKs' pattern was a WebHID/Chrome-side artifact (e.g. dispatched to two internal listeners), not a fact about the wire protocol. Native code should expect and require exactly 1 ACK per write, not 2.
linuxHidrawTransport.hardwareConfirmation: The full 18-report 'set time' sequence, sent with this write/read form, produced a byte-perfect ACK for every report and set the keyboard's TFT to the correct time and date -- independently reconfirmed the next morning (2026-08-11) when the keyboard's own clock had correctly ticked forward overnight to match real time, i.e. it's a genuinely running clock that was set correctly, not a static value that happened to look right once. Hour, minute, and date were all visually confirmed correct on the physical screen both times. Weekday was NOT visually confirmed -- the TFT screen has no weekday field at all (confirmed by checking), so there is nothing to look at. Weekday correctness instead rests on: the encoding logic being unit-tested against every day of the week (src/time.rs), and the device accepting the byte via a valid ACK without error -- weaker evidence than a visual check, and named as such rather than folded into the same 'confirmed' claim as hour/minute/date.

unresolved.item: finish (0x42) length byte numeric meaning (why 0x38/56, not e.g. 0x00)
unresolved.tried: confirmed as a stable constant across 3 live captures and the vendor source (`finishScreenControlDataPacket()` called with no arguments every time); the checksum formula using this constant is verified exactly. Only the semantic reason for the value 56 itself is unknown -- it does not block using this command.

unresolved.item: 2.4G dongle and Bluetooth connection modes -- whether the config interface is present/functional over either
unresolved.tried: only USB-C cable was tested this phase. Not yet checked for the other two modes.

unresolved.item: device connect/init traffic before the first command
unresolved.tried: not captured -- the hook was installed after the device was already connected and open (a prior WebHID permission grant was already in place from an earlier session). The vendor's click-handler source (scripts/vendor-source-excerpt.js) shows no reference to connection-time state, which is a weak signal there's no required init handshake, but this is not independently confirmed by capturing a fresh connect sequence.

unresolved.item: GIF save mode 0 -- decoded but never exercised
unresolved.tried: Mode 0 ('set it as the startup animation', max 64 frames) was used by every GIF test before Milestone 3 and never displayed anything: not on the GIF page, and not at power-up either (tested by unplugging and replugging the keyboard, which comes back to the home screen). This proves the KNOWN activation steps don't play mode-0 data; it does not prove no activation step exists (a different button sequence, a different page, a firmware-side trigger never tried) -- the search has not been exhaustive. Not implemented.

unresolved.item: GIF save mode 2 -- not offered by the vendor UI for this product; device-level behavior untried
unresolved.tried: Mode 2 ('save GIF to the device home page', max 42 frames, 96x64) has a different frame size and its button renders only for productId 12463; this keyboard is 12744, so the button is simply absent and was never clicked. This is narrower than 'inapplicable': nothing on the wire prevents sending mode-2-formatted bytes to this keyboard, and doing so has not been tried. What genuinely needs a 12463 unit is confirming the vendor's INTENDED mode-2 behavior, not whether this keyboard would react to the bytes at all. Not implemented -- a scope decision (speculative code for a feature this product's UI doesn't offer), not a claim that the technical question is closed.

unresolved.item: whether clear-picture also clears a stored GIF
unresolved.tried: Still untested. Milestone 4 deliberately does NOT tell users to run clear-picture after a failed GIF upload for this reason; the advice is to re-run set-gif. Milestone 7 shipped a clear-gif command, but it clears a GIF directly -- it does not answer whether clear-picture ALSO does, which remains a separate, still-open question.

unresolved.item: clear-gif's functional effect -- erasure vs. only clearing the live display
unresolved.tried: The command's 4 reports (cmd18 pair, cmd19 pair) are decoded, checksummed by hand, and all 4 are ACKed by the device -- confirmed deterministic across 3 independent captures. But an ACK only proves the device accepted the bytes, not that the stored animation is erased rather than just the live display clearing -- this repo has already been burned by exactly that gap once (switch-page gif's cmd15 bytes were correct and ACKed from Milestone 2 onward, yet the command was believed broken for two milestones because nobody had separately confirmed what the ACK couldn't tell them). The visual check -- save a GIF, confirm it plays, run clear-gif, confirm the panel goes blank, then physically disconnect and reconnect the keyboard and confirm the old GIF does not come back -- has not yet been run. Treat clear-gif as 'captured, decoded, ACKed -- not yet confirmed to persist across a reconnect' until it has.

unresolved.item: whether to implement the vendor GIF-save post-process (pn/Vr/wn)
unresolved.tried: Fully decoded from the vendor's real GIF-save call site (Milestone 7 follow-up, see PROTOCOL.md): pn() is an unconditional edge-aware denoise pass; Vr(image, .25) is a second, separate edge-aware local-contrast/sharpen pass gated by the same 'sharpen' toggle that already drives this repo's pre-placement fabric Convolute sharpen(); wn() is the GIF path's RGB565 packer and performs Floyd-Steinberg error-diffusion dithering, unlike the picture path's packer (te() / this repo's rgb565_encode), which truncates with no dither on both vendor sides. None of the three touches the wire -- same category as the Milestone 6 sliders and Milestone 7 placement setting. Not implemented -- a product decision on GIF visual fidelity (this repo's GIFs will show more banding and less post-resize sharpening than the vendor's own upload until this is implemented or the gap is accepted), not a claim the technical question is closed.

fixtureSchemaNote: Every report in fixtures/*.json carries these required keys: transaction_id, command_index, fragment_index, direction, hid_method, report_id, payload_hex. fragment_index is always 0 for every report in this phase's fixtures -- discovery found opcodes 0x40/0x41/0x42 are independently complete report types, not fragments requiring reassembly (see $schema_note above), so the field exists per the fixture schema but carries no ordering information here.
